question: How would rotating a tic-tac-toe board 90 degrees change the rules of the game and its strategy?

Rotating a standard tic‑tac‑toe board 90° doesn’t change the game in any substantive way.

## Rules
- **Winning condition is unchanged.** “Three in a row” (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) remains exactly the same after rotation.
- **All legal moves are unchanged.** You still choose an empty square; the set of empty squares is just relabeled.
- **Lines map to lines.** What used to be a “top row” becomes a “right column,” diagonals remain diagonals, etc. So every winning line before rotation corresponds to a winning line after rotation.

Formally: rotating the board is a symmetry of the game. It’s just a one-to-one relabeling of positions.

## Strategy
Strategy is also unchanged, except for perspective:
- **Equivalent opening moves stay equivalent.**
  - Center is still center (it’s fixed under rotation).
  - Corners rotate into corners; edges rotate into edges.
- **Any strategy transfers by rotation.** If you have a perfect response to an opponent’s move in one orientation, rotating both moves 90° gives an equally perfect response in the rotated orientation.
- **No new advantages appear.** Optimal play still leads to a draw; the standard strategic priorities (take center, create/stop forks, etc.) remain identical.

## When rotation *would* matter
Only if your rules depend on an external direction (e.g., “top row scores extra,” gravity, or a time/turn rule tied to specific labeled squares). In ordinary tic‑tac‑toe, there’s no such directional bias, so rotation changes nothing beyond labels.
